cells.tense: The thing is finished and you are still here with it.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Take the next stretch of this push at your own pace for a few days. Don't go back over the ground you covered and don't check how it's landing. What the stretch shows you, it shows you when it's done.
cells.core:
You built something and it's done, and you're still here with it. That's the uncommon part. People finish and leave, or finish and can't let go, and you're doing neither — the completed thing sits with you and the next push gets your whole weight rather than leftovers. Anybody working alongside you would see a person at ease in the work, not someone straining to hold it up.

The next stretch of this one, go at your own pace for a few days without checking in on anyone's read of it. No circling back over the ground you covered. You already took the hard part; this is where the work itself tells you that you did.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things and remain at ease in them.
cells.verb: standing at what your own effort built
cells.place: on a road with a destination and resistance in it

cells.tense: You will be watching the far end for a verdict that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Sit once this week with your hands empty and nothing queued up, and let whatever shows up show up without filing it under anything. Then get up.
cells.core:
You're standing at the far end of a piece of work, already fixing what comes next, already reading results that aren't in. Wherever the momentum goes, some part of it is checking what the finished thing says about you. That is exacting and it keeps you earning an outcome that is already yours. The last mile runs longer than the whole road did, because you're watching for a verdict nobody has handed down.

Sit once this week with your hands empty and nothing queued. Whatever arrives — a sound, a mood, a blank — let it arrive and don't sort it. Then get up and go on with your day. The worked-out thing does not get smaller while you look away, and the push will still be there when you come back to it.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing at the far end for a verdict that hasn't come.
cells.verb: standing at what your own effort built
cells.place: on a road with a destination and resistance in it

cells.tense: The push went on without you and you are still at the starting line.
cells.act: notice what is before your eyes before naming it
cells.ask: Set something you made where you can see it and look at it before you say anything about it, inside or out — just what's there. Then stop. No verdict.
cells.core:
There's a stretch of road behind you that you didn't walk. Other people close their own loops and you watch, and looking straight at your own work went quiet and stiff somewhere along the way. The momentum that used to be here isn't, and you stand near the work instead of in it. That standing is not nothing, but it has no charge in it.

Set something you made where you can see it and look at it before you say anything about it, even inside your own head — just what's there. Then stop, and don't decide whether it's good. You're not grading it. You're seeing your own hands' work with the lights on, and that is where the current starts again.
cells.sheetLine: Your work is behind you and you haven't looked at it.
cells.verb: standing at what your own effort built
cells.place: on a road with a destination and resistance in it

cells.tense: You are carrying the result as luck while your hands are still on the wheel.
cells.act: see the thing as if for the first time
cells.ask: Look at what you finished the way a stranger would — no history, no credit, no explaining. Plain looking, then keep what you noticed to yourself.
cells.core:
The push here is steady and the shape it took came out of a thousand small calls you made along the way. Asked how it worked out, you say it went all right — good timing, conditions were right, that sort of thing. The calls were yours. They're filed under circumstance, and the file has quietly become the story.

Look at what you finished the way a stranger would — no history, no credit, no explaining. Plain looking, and then keep what you noticed to yourself. The object stays the same; the only thing that changes hands is who's holding the name for it.
cells.sheetLine: The shape it took came out of your calls, and you file it as luck.
cells.verb: standing at what your own effort built
cells.place: on a road with a destination and resistance in it

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a finished thing is actually standing in this person's life — the record only says a material cycle has reached completion, not that anyone else can see it or that it is any good. The reader could reasonably say the work is not finished, it is abandoned, and they would still be describing the same card from the other side; so the ask is built to survive that, since it only asks what of the thing is still true, which is answerable either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'what was willed into being now stands' — it is the record's own line, it is beautiful, and it belongs on glass nowhere.
